title: What an artifact says about ITSELF -- the first and highest of the two declaration sites (ADR-019 decision 1)
description: The contract for the block a document opens with. It is the ONLY site that can reach the authority no place may confer, and it is therefore the only site that can be wrong about one: a place row is a human's statement about a location, and this is a human's statement about the thing itself. The grammar a reader accepts is deliberately tiny -- one field per line, a scalar or a block list, no nesting and no expression -- because a declaration carries no behaviour (Cardinal IV) and a parser that guesses at a line it does not know produces a declaration nobody wrote. A block that cannot be read is NAMED as unreadable; it is never treated as a document that declared nothing, because those are two different states and only one of them is anybody's fault. ABSENT IS LEGAL: a document with no block at all is unclassified, which is a declared state that is counted and left exactly where it is -- nothing in this kit writes this block, and a `kind` no human chose is testimony wearing a field name.

schema_version.description: The version of this CONTRACT (ADR-009), carried here because every registered schema must be able to say which version it is. It is NOT a field an author writes: a front-matter block is a human's sentence about a document, and version 1 is the version it has by saying nothing. Declared and not required, so an absent version means the first one -- which is the only thing it could mean.

kind.description: What this document IS: the id of one `kinds` row of the record-keeping vocabulary. Its PLANE is not written here and never may be -- a document that named both could contradict itself, and the plane is an attribute of the kind (ADR-019 decision 3).

authority.description: How much this document BINDS: the id of one `authorities` row. A place may cap this and may never supply it, so a document that omits it binds nothing whatever its neighbours claim. The one state no place may declare is reachable here and nowhere else.

owns.description: The topic id this document is the one owner of -- required of a document claiming the authority no place may confer, and meaningless without it: a settled answer that does not say what question it settles cannot be held against a second one. Two documents owning one id is a refusal, not a tie.

supersedes.description: The document(s) this one replaced, by host-relative path. Stated at BOTH ends or it is not stated: the other document must answer with `superseded_by`, because a succession written once leaves two documents internally correct and the pair contradictory.

superseded_by.description: The document(s) that replaced this one, by host-relative path. The other end of `supersedes`, and subject to the same two-way rule -- a reader who arrives at the old text is carried to the new one instead of obeying it.

indexes.description: The place this document is the INDEX of, by the path its corpus-map row declares. Declared here so the contract has one home; the completeness of an index in both directions is a later slice's invariant and nothing reads this field yet.

unlanded_removals.description: How many removals from THIS artifact were preserved in the record and curated nowhere (ADR-020 decision 2). A bounded artifact holds position only; what leaves it is journalled before it leaves, and a removal that states no landing is legal, honest and COUNTED -- so the count stands on the surface that shows position, where whoever is spending the record can see the bill. Written by the artifact's own writer as part of an accepted write, never by a gate and never by hand; capped, if a host chooses to cap it, by a budget row over the measure of the same name. A STRING of digits and not an integer: front matter interprets nothing by design -- the grammar reads one scalar per line and never types it -- so an `integer` here would be a contract the medium cannot satisfy, and the arithmetic belongs to the passage that owns the field.

read_when.description: The task triggers that pull this document into context, in the words a task actually arrives in. The same field, spelled the same way, as on a records-map and a corpus-map row -- one vocabulary for retrieval, never a second `answers` word. Declared here; projected by a later slice.
